utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President. I would like to introduce Ms. Nora Fredstie, from Norway, who is one of our legal interns who will be joining us this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Further Examination by Mr. Nicholls: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to quickly finish off with the video we were watching, Mr. Pirocanac's raw footage. We stopped yesterday at 56:23. There are about six more minutes, not much but we will just finish it off.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could start playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We stopped at 57:08.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blaszczyk, all I want to ask you is: Where are we now? We just passed the stadium. We can see this mosque. When we left off yesterday we saw an aerial view of Srebrenica. This photo corresponds to B on page 74 of your map book -- of your road book, excuse me. Could you just tell me where we are at this point, which direction are Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin travelling.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are leaving -- Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin, they are leaving Srebrenica. They are heading towards Potocari and Bratunac. In fact, they just passed the stadium in Srebrenica. They are on the edge of Srebrenica. This settlement is called Vidikovac or Gostilj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Keep playing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stopping now at 59:13.3. It's a bit blurry, but we can see the white barrier that says "UN" on it. Just to orient us, still heading now from Srebrenica to Potocari, where are we right now?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are right now in front of the UN DutchBat, and we passed Potocari. We passed bus compound. We saw the bus compound on the right-hand side. We saw the Feros building and now we are in front of UN DutchBat, the main gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can play, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. This is just about at the end. Do you know where this video is from? Do you remember this now?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Mr. Petrovic Pirocanac, it was recorded on the Serbian side already this -- this footage, and I didn't find this location. In fact, I didn't look for this location at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for completeness, let's play to the end. It's another minute or so, and then we'll have seen the entire raw footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stop. We can stop. Thank you, Your Honours, that concludes this part of my direct. I would tender the road book, 03931, and the CD presentation, the 360 interactive, which Mr. Blaszczyk has demonstrated, 03932.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The last part of in the road book is mosque Azemina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we heard about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't have him describe it. I stopped at the location --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What significance does it have? Is it one of the cultural monuments listed in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's not listed, Your Honours, in Schedule D. However, the video shows that on the 14th of July, it was intact after all the combat was over and afterwards it was destroyed. So I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Uh-huh, now I understand. Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be all admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 03931 will be Exhibit P4270, and 65 ter 03932 will be Exhibit P4271.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, I'd like to switch gears completely now and as quickly, as briefly as we can, go over what you can tell us about the way the so-called Drina Corps collection of VRS documents came into possession of the OTP; okay?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that process?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, can you just describe what the Drina Corps collection is and how large it is, what we mean when we say the Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drina Corps collection, Your Honour, this is archive of Drina Corps. This document from archive from Drina Corps we call it Drina Corps collection. The archive was seized by Serbian MUP and members of MOD, I mean the Serbian RS MUP and the members of MOD of RS, on the territory of Republika at that time, Serbia and Montenegro, and the collection was handed over to the OTP on the 13 of December, 2004, and arrive, in fact, the collection arrived to The Hague it was January 2005. The collection containing about 350.000 pages of documents, as far as I remember about 360 maps, and more than 3.500 -- about 3.500 photographs. The document -- the documents from the collection are documents from Drina Corps units from Drina Corps -- are documents from Drina Corps and also documents from Drina Corps units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you just tell us briefly how did the Office of the Prosecutor first hear about this collection and that it was going to be made available to us hopefully?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we received this information from the liaison office from The Hague, from Mr. Trifun Jovicic, that the collection was seized or obtained by the members of MUP of RS and MOD on 9 December 2004. And on our request, the collection was taken to the premises of RS MUP in Banja Luka and kept over there. And then after few days, after some negotiations or after some discussion with us, the collection was transported to our field office in Banja Luka. It was on the 13 of December 2004, and after checking or repacking the collection to other boxes, the entire collection was taken first to Zagreb field office on the 17 December 2004. At that time, at this time on this stage I was present in Zagreb. I was waiting for the collection to arrive from Banja Luka, and when the truck containing the documents arrived to Banja Luka, we unloaded the truck. We repacked again the documents from -- from one boxes to another boxes. I made a kind of initial review of these documents, very rough, really, because it was -- as I said, there were 350.000 pages, and we repacked to another 55 boxes and we sent this collection to -- to The Hague. And the collection was processed in The Hague starting from January 2005.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just show you a few documents relating to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 03372, please. That's the 65 ter number. While it's coming up I'll say this is a Ministry of Defence document from the Republika Srpska dated 8 December 2004. It's signed by Milovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told nothing has been uploaded on that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I check, Your Honour? It's my mistake. It's my mistake, Your Honour. I'm sorry. 03772.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we don't need to go through these documents in too much detail, Mr. Blaszczyk, because I think they're fairly self-explanatory, but can you just tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is decision of Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence signed by Minister of Defence Milovan Stankovic appointing the commission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you speak into the microphone for the benefit of interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. This is document -- this is decision signed by Minister of Defence of RS Milovan Stankovic at that time appointing the commission for taking over sealing and handing over the archive material of the Army of Republika Srpska located in Serbia and Montenegro. And this decision is -- this decision the -- the members of the commission are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I tender that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P4272, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to bring up another document, 03773. This document is dated 8 December. It's from the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, order for an official trip. Can you please -- same thing, Mr. Blaszczyk, tell us what this is and what it's about.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is document signed by the head of Main Staff of VRS. It's ordered for the commission -- the trip ordered for the commission in charge of taking over and handing over the records of the Army of Republika Srpska located in Serbia also the same people are listed as the previous documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. These are preparations for obtaining the archive?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. The document is dated 8 December 2004, the day before the -- the trip took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I tender that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4273, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: 03374, please, a similar document, this time from the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence. It's entitled "Approval of official trip abroad."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Same question, just if you could tell us briefly what this is about.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is decision of approval of the official trip abroad for the members of the commission appointed before by minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I tender that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P4274.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document 03775, also from 8 December 2004. This one from 8 December 2004, RS General Staff. What do we have here, Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is record of receipt of receiving of archive material. It was -- in fact this, record was prepared on the 8th of December, 2004, but it was signed by the members of the commission as the people who received the material and signed by the member of Army of Serbia and Montenegro who handed over this archive to this commission. And it was signed on 9 December 2004.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I tender that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted as Exhibit P4275.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, if I could have, please, 03768. This is a document from the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior again about these archives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell us a little bit about this report, Mr. Blaszczyk, signed by Dragi Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the report stated 10 January 1995, signed by Dragi Milosevic. Dragi Milosevic at that time, as far as I remember, was the head of criminal administration of RS MUP. He described in this document -- or he put the information how -- how the archive was received, how -- how they come to information about this archive and how the archive was transported to -- to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I tender that, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted as Exhibit P4276.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to make it clear, when these archives arrived in Banja Luka, they were then transported by our staff from our field office in Banja Luka to our field office in Zagreb, and that's where you joined the process and took part in cataloguing and bringing the material back to The Hague; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct. The first material was taken to Banja Luka in -- in the cases or cages used by army. There were 16 boxes, big boxes, and when the material was taken to our field office in -- in Banja Luka, we repacked -- I mean my colleagues from the field office repacked the documents to another boxes and it was sent to Zagreb on the 17 December 2004. I was present at this moment in Zagreb. I was waiting for the material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 03769, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what this document is before we go through the next few pages.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is declaration of -- this is receipt signed by our -- our investigator, field investigator, OTP investigator Finn Tollefsen. This is receipt for the 16 boxes which were received from -- from minister of defence and minister of interior containing the material -- that seized material, the Drina Corps collection. But I would like to explain something. On the bottom of this page, my colleague from the field office he mentioned here that the boxes were repacked into 24 cardboard boxes. In fact he made small mistake because, in fact, the entire collection was repacked to -- into 23 cardboard boxes, and these 24 cardboard boxes contains another material seized and also handed over by RS MUP to OTP but day after, on the 14 December 2004.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that additional box and that additional seizure, did it have anything to do with the Drina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This material handed over to the OTP on 14 December 2004, this is totally different material not connected to Drina Corps collection. This is material seized by RS MUP in one of the location in Serbia, I believe in Bijeljina. Mostly there were tapes, video-tapes and audiotapes --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but not at all connected with Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Why were the big boxes received from the RS MUP repacked into smaller cardboard boxes before going to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- these big boxes they were boxes used for ammunition for -- for keeping ammunition, weapon, and they were military boxes. We decided to repack these boxes into cardboard boxes. Also big one, unfortunately, in the -- in Banja Luka field office and this is why we had to repack it again in Zagreb because it was -- this -- the material was too heavy to keep them in these cardboard boxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What does that EOD or EOP means?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Explosive ordnance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Disposal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Disposal, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This means that the boxes were checked by UFOR team whether there is -- there are no unexploded material planted in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could go to the next page quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this here?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is confirmation signed by head of the office, our office in Zagreb, Thomas Osorio at that time. And he's confirming here that on the 17th December 2004 the Zagreb office, ICTY office, received 24 cardboard boxes from the ICTY office in Banja Luka, and it's also Thomas Osorio put here information here that these boxes were inspected and repacked into 27 boxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Twenty-seven or 57?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, 57.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go to the next page, please. Same question, can you tell us what we see here as part of our records?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is -- this is the record of how we repack the boxes, the 20 -- in fact, 23 boxes which we received from -- from Banja Luka field office containing the Drina Corps collection because, as I said before, these 24 boxes contained at that time this -- another material seized in other operation by RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page and then the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the second --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go back a page, you can explain.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second page of -- of the same document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next page, please. Okay, this is a UN ICTY cargo manifest that's got part of it redacted. Can you just tell us what this is and why the one part was redacted out?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is UN ICTY cargo manifest prepared for the person who -- who transported this material to The Hague, and this redacted part of this -- this -- this document, this is redacted because this UN ICTY cargo manifest contains also another material not related to the evidence, not related to the Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it personal effects of the --

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- staff member?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as well personal belongings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, could we go to the next page. Can you just tell us what this is and what the different signatures mean.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this is packing list. Also here is the -- listed are the boxes containing the Drina Corps collection and also these two additional boxes containing another material seized by RS MUP. It was on the left-hand side, on the bottom of this page we have the signature of the head of the mission, and I see on the right-hand side this is signature of the member of evidence unit here in The Hague. It means that member of evidence unit received this material on the 4th of January, 2005.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I tender that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4277, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, just before we finish, did you show any of these Drina Corps documents, documents seized in the Drina Corps collection, which had signatures on them to persons who authenticated their signatures, looking at the original and said, "Yes that's my signature. I remember signing this piece of paper"?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since 2005 we showed a lot of all of these documents, you know, this collection, to many of our witnesses and few of them they recognise, of course, their signature handwritings and even they could remember the contents of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just as an example, I'd like to bring up 65 ter 02064. Your Honours, I had not notified this document to be used with the witness. I have notified the Defence and spoken to them about it. So I apologise for not having that listed and thank my friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a vehicle work log of -- with the names Dusan Vucetic on it and Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic from the Drina Corps collection. It's several pages long, but just looking at this cover page, can you tell us if you recall showing this to Mr. Vucetic and what his reaction was?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to object to this testimony more as a matter of principle. You may recall that in the Milosevic case there was an Appeals Chamber decision on the admissibility of Prosecution investigators' evidence in which they held that an investigator, like the one we have testifying here, would not be allowed to testify to what other witnesses had told them because it would circumvent Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Do you mean to tender this document through this witness or just are you trying to lay some foundation as to the Drina Corps collection as a whole?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, both, Your Honour. In fact, I would make an offer of proof that Mr. Blaszczyk interviewed this person who authenticated this document by saying, "Yes, that's my signature. That's my name. That's my signature. I wrote on this document." I mean, I think that's perfectly permissible. It is hearsay but it's not circumventing Rule 92 bis for the investigator to say, "I received this document through the RS MUP as part of the Drina Corps collection. I brought it to a person who is named on document, who appears to have written on the document, and they confirmed that, yes, they had written on the document and that their signature was there."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How many documents are you trying to tender in that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have anything to add, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this comes squarely within the decision. The proper procedure would be for them to -- to tender that witness's statement under Rule 92 bis or perhaps we would cross-examine that witness if we felt that it was necessary. So while it is -- I recognise that it's one document, it's not an earth-shattering factual issue, but as a matter of principle, I think the Chamber should follow the direction of the Appeals Chamber and not allow the witness to circumvent Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I take it you are not challenging the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could just add one point, Your Honours. It's a little bit different. This is the interview. I'm not trying to tender the interview. I'm not trying to enter the witness's entire statement or information. It's one discrete point which goes directly to authentication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I see the point, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber doesn't think that Mr. Blaszczyk is going to summarise the evidence of the third party, just -- and admitting this document is not in breach of the authority in the view of the Chamber. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll give a number for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4278, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Karadzic, do you have cross-examination for this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Excellency, though I will try to be as short as possible. Good morning, Your Excellencies. I wish a good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And good morning to you, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please pull up in e-court map number 6 from this binder that was admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You mean the map in the road book. Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the page number, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0618-4127. But this map was dubbed number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or my apologies, 73.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 73.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, can we agree that the Srebrenica-Bratunac road is oriented more or less north/south, or south/north, to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that mosque on this Vitlovac hill which is elevation 553?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked this -- this mosque with number 21. Exactly where we have 21 and this yellow circle with black dot in, this is the mosque, the location of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then that would not be Vitlovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Gostilj, Gostilj, and I know that the locals they are calling this settlement Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see, thank you. We can agree, can we, that the sun -- or, rather, the daylight moves from east via south towards the west. In other words, east, south-east, south, south-west, west; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. I'm not -- yes. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Even in Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to take a look at this image on page 74. Do you agree, Mr. Blaszczyk, that this mosque does not have a roof, or, rather, a dome as is customary at this elevation? In other words, not even in July was there a dome there or a roof.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. On this picture the mosque has no roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this is a still from that video; correct. Fifty-seven minutes, 4 seconds; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is a still from the video, Petrovic video, on his way back from Zeleni Jadar, Srebrenica to Serbian territory. And if I may point something also that I don't know whether anybody pay attention, but when Mr. Petrovic together with Mr. Borocanac -- Borovcanin, sorry, they were driving to Srebrenica on the 14, and there was discussion in the car. They discussed about the mosque. It was -- they discussed this mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can also agree that on the two visible sides of this building we can see four windows on each side; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have page 75, please. To me, this does not appear to be the same building. The windows are different.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, definitely it's the same building. I've been there several times. I talked to the owner of the land where the mosque is located and definitely this is the same building. This was only mosque in this area at that time. I know quite well the history of this mosque. I know that this is the first mosque built before the war - I don't remember the year exactly - but built on the private land and I think even paid by the private person. And the son of the man who -- whose land is over there is still living in this house next to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But would you agree, for instance, that on the photograph on the right-hand side, even the one on the left-hand side, it all looks a bit different? Now, if you look at the number of windows, for instance, and the shot was from the right-hand side of the road, in other words, Srebrenica-Bratunac, that's on the right side; correct, of the road?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. This picture is not so very clear. You know, it's not the best quality especially if we play -- this is not very best quality. But I would like to point one -- one situation. That picture A from the page 74, this is the edge of the stadium in Srebrenica, when we are leaving Srebrenica, and I made the picture 1 from the page 75 almost from the same location. Okay. The wall of the stadium is not visible here but the picture is done almost in the same location. And the second picture from the page 75 is done from the direction of Potocari. It's -- it means from another side, from the south -- from the north part of the road. But picture one from the south part of the road. From the north, we have the picture number 2 on the page 75. It may looks little bit different than the footage, the stills from Petrovic video, because this is different direction, different perspective. This is my explanation, but definitely it's the same mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please look at this. If you are on this Srebrenica-Bratunac road, we see on page 74 two sides, two walls of the building, and we can see the same wall -- walls from the same road. In other words, the shot could not have been taken from the north-east. It could have been done either from south-east or from north-west. Now, can we take a look at page 76, please. And may I ask you who was your guide here? Who directed you which way to go?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a guide for myself. I was the guide there. I had no guide. I had interpreter with me, but that's it. It was me who decided where to go and what to see. I -- in spite of having interpreter with me, I'm more familiar with this area than the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see and can you agree that here, too, we see more openings on the wall and their distribution is a bit different?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this mosque is totally destroyed, in fact. We see only one wall, you know, just a few walls over there, but the inside is burnt, destroyed, blew up, and we have no minaret here. It's totally different shape than it was in July 1995 when Mr. Petrovic recorded this mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk, but I am wondering about the walls. The walls of this structure, they have more openings than the structure that we saw on that film much so I was wondering whether you were taken to some other location?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guarantee that this is the same location recorded by Mr. Petrovic. This is -- what can I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now have page 21, map 5, please. Mr. Blaszczyk, can we agree that the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road -- or, rather, Kravica-Konjevic Polje road lies more or less in the direction -- or runs from east to west; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree, then, that in the course of the day, at different parts of the day, the shades or the shadow projected by daylight or by the sun can only be towards the west or north-west, north or north-easterly; correct? In other words, it would be opposite to the side where the sun is, because the sun moves from east to south and then west, and the shadows that would be projected would be on the opposite side towards the north; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now have page 46, please. Let's take this -- let's take a look at the photograph at 17:53:09. Here it would appear that the sun is north-west, and that's not possible; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't make an experiment. You know, I don't know whether it's possible or not, but also I'm convinced and 100 per cent sure that this is the location I spotted in my book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All I'm trying to do is establish the accuracy of this video material and the orientation. Now, if Kravica goes in this direction and Konjevic Polje is in the other direction, then we should have the front left side, the sun -- that should be the sunny side and not the other way round. It couldn't be where it is; correct? Now, if you take at the look at the photograph at the bottom, below, we have the same situation. The sun cannot be more northerly in relation to the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. It should be southerly; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not necessarily. Depends, you know, how high the sun was at that time. I think it was about 0400 hours when they stopped in this area. But really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a curved road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is a curved road as well, and it can mislead us a little bit, but to be sure, we should -- should make the same experiment on the spot, you know, on the same hours, the same day, but -- but I am sure that this is not [indiscernible] with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But can we put it this way probably: Can you tell from this picture Konjevic Polje is in which direction, only from this image.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From this image Konjevic Polje is direction -- the west direct, to the west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question is whether you can tell the exact direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, but this is curve --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You know the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I know the road very well. Yes, it is marked here the direction to Konjevic Polje, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, irrespective of this curve and how sharp it is, unless it was a hairpin curve, the sun cannot be more northerly or northerly -- west-northerly in relation to the road which runs this way and the shadow should be south -- north-easterly; correct? If it can be of assistance, perhaps we can take a look at page 36. Please look at the bottom right photo, 14:57:19. Can you see how the shadow is projected, how these vehicles project the shadow? It is to the south; correct? And this is a correct orientation. They're going towards Konjevic Polje, and the sun is to the left and forward, and the shadow then would be to the right and backward; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knowing the shape of this road, rather, it would be towards east and north, the shadow. But really I cannot comment on it because I should be there just to measure the shadow if it's necessary, but we didn't see at that time that it's necessary at all. The location has been found, the video authenticated by Mr. Petrovic and by other people, by other witnesses. We didn't see any reason why to -- to -- to check additional confirmation that -- about the shadow, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you cannot really bribe the sun. It is completely unbiased. So all I'm trying to do is use these materials and see how useful they can be as presented here. My -- it is my suggestion that this orientation, the orientations here shown are not accurately established, and as we can see on the bottom right photograph on page 36, it shows there that Konjevic Polje is forward and the sun projects this shadow to the back and north. However, that's not the case with the other photos; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said, you know, this is not straight road. There are a lot of bends, a lot of curves, and in my book I marked the direction where we are heading Konjevic Polje or Bratunac. It's not necessary is reflect this -- this reflects west and east. I didn't have compass with me. I couldn't say, you know, just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look at page 50, please. The upper left picture you see Kravica and Bratunac are behind, in the background of the picture, and the sun is shining from the direction of the south-west and the shadow falls north-west. This is well determined, well established, and the other cannot be well established.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this -- but this is -- as I said, this is on another bend, you know. It's not -- not in the straight direction to Kravica to Bratunac exactly on the -- on west. This is different location. You're right, but taking into consideration the bend, the curves, it's difficult to say right now without -- without making experiment, you know, how it goes on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can a curve be so important that the sun would shine from the right side of the road? From the north side.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends which direction the road leading us. In spite that we are going to the -- to the west, for example, first we can get the road leading us to the north or to the south and then turning again to the west. General direction to Konjevic Polje is west, but the road is -- there are a lot of bends and sometimes we are going to the north, sometimes to the south, sometimes to the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we look from Kravica, Konjevic Polje is slightly to the north-west, not exactly north; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you observe these headbands worn by some people in several cases?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice that some of the fighting men have an armband and one of them even has a band on the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the picture, you know, what we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at page 48 for the head, and I will point out the shoulder on the video material. I will state the exact minute. You remember this. It's not only this man. There are several fighters who wear the same.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This man is a member of the 1st PJP Company from CJB Zvornik. I'm referring to the man from the picture A.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm still looking for the reference in the video footage for the armband and the shoulder. Do you remember that, at one point, one of the troops or the policeman told one Muslim young man to take his T-shirt off? How did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was a military T-shirt?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looked like military T-shirt. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was not taken from him. He was just told to take it off, and he continued on his way holding the T-shirt in his hand; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The portion we see that the policeman told the man to take -- take his T-shirt off, but it was not taken from him, yes. We don't see it on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree it was a suggestion for his own benefit to remove any sign of belonging to the military? [It actually benefits that young man. It's for his good.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense? What kind of benefits could be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that he be treated as a civilian, not potentially as a fighter who took that T-shirt off a dead Serb. Did that ever cross your mind?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, rather, the man with the military or quasi-military T-shirt could expect that could be treated as a POW at that time and he surrendered to the army and I don't see any reason why not. It would be better for him. And please take into consideration at that time it was July 1995, and it was very, very hot outside. It was sunshine, and sitting on the meadow for a few hours without T-shirt is quite risky for your health. I don't see that it was done on -- the person who asked the young man to took off his T-shirt he meant any benefit for this young man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Blaszczyk, that during three and a half years the Serb population around the enclave was being killed and that it was all done by local men? Both Serbs and Muslims there were local residents. Do you really think that it was not about personal vendettas at least in some cases? Did you find or look for any information about that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know that sometimes the Muslim forces also committed the crimes on the Serb population. This is -- we are not disputing it. But I didn't look inside these crimes very carefully because I was involved in another investigation, the Srebrenica investigation, the crimes related to the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But if the Muslim forces had committed crimes, wouldn't it have been better for that young man to take off the T-shirt designating him as a member of those forces that had committed crimes? If it's a complicated question, we'll leave the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Blaszczyk answered that question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Blaszczyk. In this video, at 39:35.2 you say -- in fact, we see the insignia of the Drina Wolves. However, there is an armband on one of the young men and on another fighter we see a band on the left shoulder. That's at 41:48. Shall we play it or do you remember that section?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember. You're referring to the man walking in Srebrenica town; is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are three of them. One of them is wearing a flak jacket. He has the insignia of Drina Wolves on his arm, and another has a red band on his shoulder, whereas the third one has a headband. The red band is seen on 47:44.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, but I would like to see the footage from this part to be sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then play it at 47 -- sorry. No, first 39:35. Let's start from that. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He has something on his left arm; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the man on the middle?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is patch of Drina Wolf.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Play it back, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What he says about the army fleeing in all directions into the woods, does that refer to the Muslim troops?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in response to a question from Mr. Nicholls, who was being shot at, who was in that column, you said the Muslim population. I suppose it was a slip of the tongue. Do you agree that the overwhelming majority of that column of 13- to 15.000 people were soldiers, not civilians?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the properly armed soldiers with uniforms? I don't agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I mean those who are capable of killing regardless of what they're wearing. A person, a man, can wear a ballerina's tutu. If he has a gun and he's trained to use it, he can kill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber will not rely on Mr. Blaszczyk's evidence as to the nature of that column. Please move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we play another tape, or maybe we'll skip that part where a red band is seen around the arm -- or the shoulder. 44:20. We can play on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see in the previous passage the armband on the left arm? We can rewind a little.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the difference of 4 seconds, we may go back to 44:15 and start. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just want to say we've done this before. If Mr. Karadzic can say stop in English when he wants us to stop, that helps Mr. Reid hit the button more quickly and not wait for translation. Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree this is a white armband on the left arm?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is little bit different. This is Ljubisa Borovcanin. We have his photo also from the day before, from the 13th of July, 1995. He had the same badge. This is the badge of the Special Police Brigade. It's visible also on his left arm on the 13 July 1995 in Potocari. It's much more clear and visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just wanted to put on the record, for this discussion we are at 44:22.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. While leaving this image there, can we upload page 14 of the road book. Mr. Blaszczyk, do you mean this patch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct, Your Honour. I mean this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the two armbands are identical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see what's at 44:20 -- sorry, a moment. 44:20. Yes, that's it. Just a moment. 47:40.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree this soldier has a red band on his left shoulder?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I see it, everybody see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that those were usual demarcations, usual markings for soldiers in combat to avoid friendly fire?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know. Could be red, could be white, depends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Today we're not sitting in an extended format, and it's time to take a break if it is convenient.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just being told about that by my associate. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a break for 20 minutes and resume at 20 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice, Mr. Blaszczyk, that Mane Djuric said, and that's at 1.38 -- could we see 1.38 where Pirocanac says he's filming for the police. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we play this part of the video, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 01:38.1. Rewind just a little so we can hear the words.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard him saying he was filming for the police, and I will find the spot where Mane Djuric is speaking. I believe it comes soon. Play on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since -- is it not page 12 of the road book? It says five minutes something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure, Your Excellencies. It should be closer to the spot where it said he's filming for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Mane Djuric saying that UNPROFOR should go and see if anyone else wants to leave and that's their job? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to -- to play it again if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's start at 5:55.4. I believe Djuric says that to a Serb, because his words are, "They should go. It's their job."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I believe if we beginning playing at approximately 4:16, we will get there, to the part Mr. Karadzic is looking for.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that it is Djuric's understanding it was the UNPROFOR's job to go and see if anyone else wants to come and to bring those who want to leave?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see the words and we hear Mane Djuric. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that? Did you remark that that was the distribution of jobs?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remark what Mane Djuric said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you check to whom those houses belonged? With so many destroyed houses, were they destroyed at the time or earlier, the ones we saw on the film?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the houses in Potocari or where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All along the road in that area you could see on the film a lot of destroyed houses. Were they destroyed recently relative to the moment we see on the movie or much earlier? To whom those houses belonged?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know they were mixed houses, Serbs and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we agree that at 1:00 you saw some people going back, coming back? Did you understand that those were Serbs returning to Srebrenica? And later on you saw interviews. Were those people to whom Pirocanac was speaking Serbs?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, can we play this part of the video? I would like to see exactly what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 01.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. No. Further, further, at the later part, in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not 00, but 01.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We're not clear on the time Mr. Karadzic wants.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 01.00, not 00.13. 01.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What, in your understanding, do we see here? Who are these people either moving in or coming back?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they are Serbs, and the area when this was recorded, this is near Bratunac, very near Bratunac, not in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They are returning to Srebrenica because Bratunac was continuously in Serb hands, whereas Srebrenica was not.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Pirocanac and Mr. Borovcanin are driving towards Bratunac, and these people are walking towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the interview you did with Mr. Pirocanac? Did he tell you that they were being shot at at the time? Look at page 34 of that interview from 2007. It says they were shooting the whole time.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember details on this interview, much details, but there was kind of information from him that there was shooting along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see 2352. Do you recall there's a man falling to the ground there? What did you understand? Was that a wounded person or was he wounded at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask if this interview from 2007 is part of the 92 bis package?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe we bis'd his -- just his testimony from the Popovic case, not previous interviews, if that's what Mr. Karadzic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then the Defence would like to tender that if there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I haven't seen it, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I think he needs to ask some questions and give more -- a greater foundation for tendering that entire interview. I -- in principle, I don't think I would object, but at this point he hasn't -- it's not clear to the witness, I think, what the question even was that he was being asked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then upload T0003261. I have the Serbian version here, and I believe we need the English one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the 65 ter number, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. It should be 04761, and unless I'm mistaken, I don't believe we've received a list yet of crossed documents. I apologise if I'm mistaken, but we don't have it, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My mistake. I thought that was part of the 92 bis package because it relates to this video material and Mr. Blaszczyk participated in the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did attend; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see page 34. That's page 34 in Serbian at least. Let's look at ZP, Zoran Petrovic, at the top. "We just stopped because they were shooting at us the whole time. We were alone on the road." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is transcript from this interview, what he said during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see page 15 so that we can correlate it with the video later. Do you remember that Borovcanin told him: "Hold on to me, stick to me, and you can film anything." And Pirocanac confirmed in this interview that he was under no restriction in his filming. On my page 15, it's the words at the bottom after Mr. Nicholls, JN, [In English] It should start: "Well, I asked him what's going on." [Interpretation] Do you remember he told you that Borovcanin had told him, "Just stick to me"? When he said, "What should I do?" Borovcanin told him there's no problem. He can film anything he likes.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find this portion in the English version, but let me check Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think that it may be one page down in English. Yes, Ljubovija bridge. Yes. That's the reference.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe next page in English version.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Please, next page to see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I ask for the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't want to interrupt, but what's the question, Judge? He -- he may be able to just answer the question if we get to it, rather than reading out from the interview --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, why don't you just put your question as suggested by Mr. Nicholls, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was there and Mr. Blaszczyk wanted to see this. Do you remember that in the interview Mr. Pirocanac informed you that Borovcanin and no one else imposed any restrictions? They could film -- or, rather, Pirocanac could film whatever he wanted; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes, but I don't remember the exact word used by Pirocanac in this interview. This is why I would like to check the transcript from the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then it must be two pages up, because it seems that there is more pages in English rather than less. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not included in his 92 bis transcript? Probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think so, Your Honour. I can't give a page reference, but he was my witness in at that trial, and I recollect him making that point that, that he was allowed to film.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: And speaking, and -- I think next -- next page. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "I asked him," row 12. [Interpretation] Line 16, please take a look at that: "[In English] And he said: Stick to me. You can film everything. I don't recall he had forbidden me to film anything."

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see. And what is the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So did you establish that he could record or film everything he wanted to film, and do you agree that then all the material was accessible to him and to you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw what was recorded at that time on this -- from his raw footage and from the broadcasted documentary from Studio B, but we are sure this is not entire material, that a few seconds are still missing. And I can say this material was accessible definitely to Mr. Pirocanac but not entire material to us. We got so kind of the redacted material from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But wasn't he saying that you had received raw material rather than redacted material, and you agree that Ms. Hajji Vukovic could not offer anything else but what Pirocanac had had? Do you remember that Ms. Hajji Vukovic wrote to the army that she wanted to hand over the material? Do you agree that it had to be this same material?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said, we received a copy of the raw material but this material handed over to us or being even accessible by us -- to us by Mr. Pirocanac was in a redacted version. There are a few sequences that are missing. They are missing the part of Kravica warehouse. They're missing the prisoners kept in the white house in Potocari. This is visible, what we know for sure for 100 per cent because we know the footage from Studio B broadcast. But we believe that there are more materials redacted. We never seen this more material which is redacted from raw material. And Mr. Karadzic mentioned here tape handed over to the security organ of Main Staff, yes, this material is also copy of the raw material but in a redacted version, without part of Kravica, for example, and white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many minutes were broadcast by Studio B out of all of this material of Mr. Pirocanac?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Studio B broadcasted documentary called "Srebrenica," I think, and entire material -- edited material, this is edited material, they choose only the best picture according to them, you know, that could be showing the TV. It lasted about half an hour, if I'm not mistaken, but I believe it is about half an hour. Including, of course, this missing portion from the raw material. But only a few seconds, just few footage of white house and few footage of warehouse in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 34 of this interview, we saw that there's this reference to shooting. Mr. Pirocanac says that he has some 20-minute material; right? "In my 28-minute material." And then he was asked whether he had stopped there, you asked him that, and he said, "No, no, they were shooting at us." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If this is in transcript, probably he said that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Except for feelings, do you not have any other basis to establish that there is something is missing; isn't that right? Do you have any proof of anything missing?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first proof is this is broadcast of Studio B that we see the footages which are not included in -- in the raw material, and then also we have a witness who saw entire material, not edited material, in Studio B. I believe it was on the 15th of July, 1995. And he saw more footages, not much more but little bit more. It's not only my feeling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that Pirocanac made the programme that was broadcast on Studio B and that he played what had been missing, rather, that he had edited it; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pirocanac, of course, took the part in editing this programme because this is his material, and he added to this programme these two parts missing from -- at least two parts missing from -- from the raw material. But I would say that he didn't include everything what is missing from the raw material in Studio B broadcast. I would not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you don't have any proof, do you? We would like to make that distinction, what you would say, what you would not say, and what you know for sure.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except the statement of the witness who saw entire material, we don't have anything more. We don't have the tape, original tape, with the entire material. We got only the reacted version of raw material and that's it. Studio B broadcast and witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have -- I can't find it in my interview. Could I have the passage Mr. Karadzic spoke of on page 37, lines 13 to 16, where he says, "On page 34 of this interview," and then he speaks about Mr. Pirocanac allegedly said something about his 20-minute, 28-minute material. I'd just like to find that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In the Serbian version on page 36 -- or, rather, 34, it says in Bratunac -- Pirocanac is saying: "In Bratunac, somewhere on the right-hand side I filmed this thing that is very important for your work," and so on and so forth, and he says: "In this 28-minute material of mine." And then there is a reference to gunfire being opened at them. So he refers to 28-minute material, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we are asking the English page for that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll find it now. We displayed it a moment ago when it said: "They fired at us." Yes, that's the page. Thank you to the person who found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he says here that he had 28-minutes material. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I quite -- I don't understand what he is talking about because 28-minutes material could be only material from Studio B, because this edited version lasted about half an hour, but his entire raw material it lasted one hour, exactly one hour and one minute maybe, or two minutes. But may I see another page of this interview? The next one, please. Well, it's difficult to tell, I mean, because this weird number, minutes. It's 28-minutes material, it's only broadcasted material, not entire raw material handed over by Mr. Pirocanac to us. We have one hour of material from him, maybe more. Of course, in redacted version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But, Mr. Blaszczyk, you had insight into the rest. Well, all right. We're going to abandon this topic altogether. Did you see the other films that were made by Mr. Pirocanac -- or, rather, the other documentaries from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For example, did you see this film about Semizovac, near Sarajevo, where the Serbs were totally encircled from the inside and the outside? That was also filmed by Christiane Amanpour for CNN.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not, but during our interview with Mr. Pirocanac, he handed over to us also one recorded documentary by him about the activities of the Special Police Brigade. As far as I remember, it was on Sarajevo front line and from June 1995. I've seen this film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's about the Black Swans, the special Muslim unit called the Black Swans.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that not. It was -- yeah. It was the film, the movie about -- about day-to-day life of -- of police brigade members in Sarajevo front line, but I don't think it was about Black Swans, not that one. At least I don't remember, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this interview, did Mr. Pirocanac inform you about the existence of such documentary films, and did you show any interest in them?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should refer to my interview. I haven't read this interview very carefully recently. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's page 9 in my version, the Serbian version. He is telling you about Christiane Amanpour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of this name perhaps it's going to be easier to find the proper page in English. So perhaps we can move on to page 10. Yes, excellent. Well found. It is exactly what we're looking at now. Oh, sorry, it's in Serbian. Perhaps the next page and perhaps we can find Amanpour there. I mean the next page in English. Yes. From line 15 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he informed you about that. Did you ask for that footage? Did the OTP show any interest whatsoever in that footage?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. We may have this footage here in The Hague, but I don't remember. In fact, I was the investigator involved in the investigation regarding the fall of Srebrenica in -- from July 1995. I was not much interested about the material from the other part of Bosnia at that time, especially this documentary probably is available for another team who -- which -- which conduct an investigation in -- in this part of the Bosnia. But I cannot answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to see 23:52.1 or 52, from that film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again I'm not objecting, but we still don't have a list of cross-examination documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is from the road book film.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought he had a different one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interview is also from the Prosecutor's list. I thought it was part of 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not 00:23, but 23:52.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us play and then see whether it's the one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can stop here for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Blaszczyk, in what direction these trucks are heading?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, these trucks are heading towards Kravica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From Konjevic Polje or from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These trucks are on the road near Sandici meadow. It means from Konjevic Polje direction towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in your view, which is the sunny side there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the sun is on the top according to -- I don't see much, much shadow here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have what I asked for, 22 -- or, rather, 23:52.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow the content, Mr. Karadzic, if this is not it. What footage do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the Sandici meadow and where Borovcanin is saying they're targeting cars, and then we see a man falling. Sandici, as far as I can tell, it's 23:52.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's what you spoke of on page 67 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe 11:20. I'm not sure. No. On page 68 there is this suggestion that someone is shooting, although there is no sound. So I would like us to see that moment when Borovcanin says they're firing at the car.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not notice this pause yesterday. There's something missing. Please let us see whether this is it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it is in this darker part. You can see a man, a Muslim in a leather jacket, and then you hear Borovcanin saying they are targeting the car, and then we see them lifting a man off the road. It must be at 11:20. And he says that on page 68 of yesterday's transcript. That's what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it's the part -- if I'm right, the part that Mr. Karadzic is looking for, if we start at 23, within about 30 seconds we'll get to the part I think he's talking about, where Mr. Borovcanin talks about cars being targeted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Stop. [Interpretation] Can we see here where Borovcanin says, "Targeting, targeting cars."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Blaszczyk, that this is in keeping with what Mr. Pirocanac said on page 34, I believe, that they were being targeted throughout the time?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that there was -- along the road there was fighting also with the Muslim forces. Except the civilians, there were soldiers, the people -- there were people -- or, rather, people who had a gun and it was also fighting. We know that the soldiers, the Serbian soldiers, at least one in Sandici meadow was killed. I believe it was on the 13. And by grenade and two or three were wounded. Yeah, I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember when Pirocanac said that he had seen Serbs and UNPROFOR members helping people? It's on page 14, 15 of the interview in the Serbian version. Do you remember that he told you that he had seen that?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is something, but if this is in transcript -- I don't remember exactly the words, but if we look at the transcript and he says in this way, this is true. What he says, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember Mr. Pirocanac telling you that Borovcanin went to visit a wounded officer in the hospital? He was in fact a military police.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, remember, but he wasn't the military police. He was the member of Sekovici Detachment, I think deputy commander of Sekovici Detachment, Cuturic.
