He was wounded in an incident in Kravica warehouse and he was transport -- he was taken to -- or went to -- to Bratunac health centre. And, yes, I remember Borovcanin went there to -- to visit him. But he wasn't military police officer. He was the member of Special Police Brigade, Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many men, how many police officers guarded these prisoners at Kravica? Do you agree that it was about five to six men who guarded several hundred men?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never established the number, exactly how many people guarded the prisoners in Kravica warehouse but -- but we know that they were members of -- of Sekovici Detachment, the people who guarded them, who took the part in killings, and some PJP people were -- members were also present in Kravica warehouse, but how many we don't know exactly. I don't know. We never be able to establish this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the wounding of this officer, did that precede the shooting of the prisoners? Did you receive information to the effect that the prisoner came up to this person to ask for fire to light his cigarette, and while -- while he was lighting his cigarette, this man pulled out a knife and then tried to stab him and then he shot back, and was it on this occasion and on that -- that the man was wounded and is this when there was shooting?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard story described in this way how you did. I never heard this story, that somebody stabbed the -- or tried to stab the policeman. No. I know that Cuturic was wounded in Kravica warehouse and they kept prisoners in Kravica warehouses. One of -- I don't remember his name now but one of these also members of Sekovici Detachment of Special Police Brigade, in fact the gun was taken from him and then one of the Muslim men kept in Kravica warehouse killed him with this gun. And then Cuturic tried to get back the gun from the Muslim man and burned his hands, and this is why he was taken to the hospital, to the health centre in Bratunac. But just after that, according to our information, the killings started in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But my learned friend Mr. Nicholls asked you about the return of Borovcanin to Bratunac. Did you understand that he went back there in order to visit this person at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think that's quite accurate that I asked about the return of Mr. Borovcanin to Bratunac. I believe what I talked about was the U-turn made on the road and then heading back in the direction of Bratunac before quite reaching Konjevic Polje, just to keep it straight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but unless I misunderstood, there was the possibility that the suggestion was made that this was because they wanted to go back to Sandici meadow. However -- well, tell us, Mr. Blaszczyk. When was this visit to the hospital? Was it before or after?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the Kravica incident started. And -- sorry, you meant that -- according to you, Mr. Borovcanin made a U-turn and went towards Sandici and Kravica and Bratunac to visit the wounded officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, would you like to discuss with this witness all the substantive matters?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. All I wanted to know is because Mr. Nicholls insisted on their turning around and going back, but looking at the shadows, I don't think that's how it was exactly. What I would like to know is: How did Mr. Blaszczyk learn when they went to the hospital for this visit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we talked to Mr. Borovcanin. You have the statement of Mr. Borovcanin. We talked to his driver, we talked to Pirocanac as well. And yes, yes, we got this information from the witnesses. And also we talked to other members of Special Police Brigade who participated, who were present during these events in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When was this visit to the hospital? Was it before they left for Konjevic Polje or after they returned?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after they returned, definitely after they made the U-turn, and we have the last footage from the raw material of Pirocanac is recorded in Sandici meadow. Then we have redacted version few seconds -- about 22 seconds where we believe the incident in Kravica was recorded, and after that Mr. Borovcanin returned to -- to -- went to Bratunac hospital to see Cuturic. And, Your Honour, if you notice, this is also in the raw material that Mr. Borovcanin is talking on the radio and talking with one of his soldiers and members of Special Police Brigade call -- his calling him by -- by nickname Oficir. This nickname Oficir, it was the nickname of Cuturic, the soldier who was wounded in the Kravica warehouse incident. I think this is conversation on the way back from -- when they made the final U-turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they made that U-turn to go to the hospital. So at the time when there was this Kravica incidence -- incident, they were in Konjevic Polje, Borovcanin and Pirocanac; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. This is not correct. They made a U-turn. They stopped at Sandici. They went towards Kravica, and they stopped in Kravica. In the meantime when they were approaching Kravica, Pirocanac recorded these events in Kravica, this few footage, we know, and after stopping in Kravica, Borovcanin went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Pirocanac told you that he did not stop at Kravica, that he filmed this from the car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should look at his interview, but we talked to Mr. Borovcanin. We talked to his driver, and we know that they stopped in Kravica. And also we -- we have the statement, I believe, other members of Sekovici Detachment who were at that place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, from the video we can see that it was shot from a moving car, don't we?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. This is the footage shot from the moving car when they approaching -- approaching Kravica warehouse from Sandici meadow, when they were driving from Sandici meadow toward Kravica warehouse. Where they stopped exactly, I think it was pointed to us by the driver of Mr. Borovcanin, where they stopped the car in Kravica warehouse. I should refer to his statement but -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, both Pirocanac and his film show that they did not stop and that the film was made while they were moving; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Pirocanac raw material and Pirocanac footage showing us that -- that they were moving towards Kravica because he recorded incident in Kravica where they are -- were approaching Kravica warehouse. We don't see on this footage that they stopped the car, but doesn't mean that they didn't stop the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one second. For clarification, Mr. Blaszczyk, did you say or did you not that you knew why they made a U-turn, the reason for their U-turn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue. Do you think you can conclude your cross-examination before the break?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When do we go on break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At noon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best. I'm not sure, but I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did know that after their return they went to the hospital. Now, where was Borovcanin when he spoke with Oficir on the radio?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the way to Sandici meadow when they made their U-turn. I believe I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was when he spoke with Oficir on the radio.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, where.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was before Sandici meadow, approaching Sandici meadow from the area of Pervani, Lolici. Still driving that few hundred metres from Sandici meadow from direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see, although there was no mention made of that, that the church in Srebrenica was roofless and did you know that it had been turned into an sty, a pigsty, a stable, as it were, and a public toilet?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It can be seen, although I won't show it now because it wasn't commented upon by the person who filmed it, but we do have it on film if we should need it. Just a moment, bear with me, please. Did you see the entire footage that Pirocanac could offer you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the raw material handed over by him to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and also whatever was broadcast on Studio B?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Studio B was in sharp opposition to President Milosevic and that they were also political and ideological opponents of ours, of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't got the details, but I know it was a kind of -- they called this Studio B as independent television in Belgrade at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move to this other topic and touch upon the Drina Corps collection. Can you tell us, please, whether you agree that that is state property, that archive.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean state property? Right now or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To put it differently, was it unlawful that for several years these archives were in private hands and they were kept in an inappropriate place?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say that the archive was in the private hands. I would say that was under the supervision -- rather, say that it was under the supervision of the 1st Army of Bosnia -- the Serbs' Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, VRS, and then ended up in the barracks of Serbia and Montenegro army in Gornji Milanovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that lawful or unlawful?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information we received from Serbia and Montenegro authorities on our request, the authorities of this country didn't know -- at least the higher officials didn't know that the archive was transported to the territory of Serbia and ended up in -- in the barracks, military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you investigate why this -- these records were unlawfully taken out of Republika Srpska and stored in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We know -- yeah. We suspect -- no, and we are pretty sure why it was taken to the Serbia across the river, because in Bosnia-Herzegovina the archive was not secure, let's say. If the archive would be in Bosnia-Herzegovina, it would be available to the ICTY. In the past, several premises of the army of VRS were searched by ICTY. It was Zvornik, Bratunac, and Drina Wolves barracks and we seized at that time some documents. It is visible that we are looking for the documents at least from the period of July 1995. And it was well known for everybody that ICTY is interested to -- to have the archive of Main Staff, archive of Drina Corps, of the units which -- at least participated in -- in operation in Srebrenica in July 1995. And this is our assumption and I think this is justified assumption that this is why the archive was transported to or moved to the Serbia territory where ICTY had no access or the international forces had no access to Serbia territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So it is your view that there was some unlawful private reasons for these archives to be moved. Did you establish what the reason was for this -- these archives to re-surface?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that the archive was moved to the territory of Serbia and Montenegro in 1999, I think in spring 1999, and then disappeared somewhere. According to our witness -- our witnesses, because we tried to locate this archive. We talked to many of the witnesses who had contact with the archives as -- when the archive was available -- was still in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we got this information that the archive was transported to -- had been transported to Serbia and Montenegro. And why this archive was discovered or handed over to us in this particular time a few years later in 2004, in December, I don't know. According to the information we received from authorities of RS in Bosnia-Herzegovina, they came to know about this archive through their own channels in -- that the archive is located in the barracks in Gornji Milanovac, and they are transportation this archive to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that in any way related to the agreement, plea agreements that were made by some accused here at The Hague, this fact that it suddenly came to the knowledge where these archives were?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will establish that when we compare the dates when one of the accused made a plea agreement. But do you know that one of the accused actually participated in this removal of the archives and then later on he reached a plea agreement here with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, but this accused participated or just to the part of -- in this action of removing this archive from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the Serbia and Montenegro. He was not aware where the archive was taken out from the place in -- in Mali Zvornik, in fact. This was -- the first archive was placed in Mali Zvornik. This is across the river from Zvornik, on the territory of Serbia and Montenegro at the time. But he was not aware where the archive ended up, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish, as you established that he took part in the removal of the archives, did you also establish whether he had any role in the discovery of these documents and their return?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had no role of -- of this action of returning these documents to -- to the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But when the archive was placed in Mali Zvornik, I think between -- if I could remember, between 1998 and 1999, this person had access to this archive, and he collected few documents from this archive and he handed over these documents over to the ICTY, to the OTP. But he didn't play any role in returning this entire archive from territory of Serbia Montenegro to Bosnia-Herzegovina in December 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you establish that? Couldn't he tell his friends where the archives were or inform them about everything else, what was -- what measures were to be taken and which were not? So did you exclude that possibility or is there -- does it exist? Does the possibility exist?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I exclude this possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you exclude it?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person had been interviewed by OTP several times and the subject of archive was touched with him also several times. And we never proved, we never got any piece of information that this person could be -- could be involved in returning this archive to the territory of -- to RS and at that time this person served his sentence, I believe. He was sentenced already by this Tribunal and he was in The Hague or wherever he was in gaol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any evidence that he participated? You got evidence that he did not -- did you maybe get evidence that he did not participate, but it was not in your interest to have it presented?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't receive any evidence that he participated in it and I -- no. We don't have -- we didn't have a piece of evidence just saying that he could participate in this -- this returning of the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you find evidence that he was not involved? Did you rule it out using the regular methods?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't understand why we should take into consideration that he was involved in this returns of this archive. What we could, we sent request to the Serbia and Montenegro. We sent also request to the authorities of RS asking about the path or the way how the archive was -- where it was hidden exactly and how it was possible that was taken to the territory of Serbia and Montenegro and how it was possible that it was returned to RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Defence would like to know all that, too, but you said yourself that the said person was involved in handling the archive. It seized certain documents illegally and transported the rest to Serbia or was involved in its transportation to Serbia. Now, what I want to know is what was the interest in making the archive disappear and then suddenly returning it. If you don't know, it doesn't matter, but did you rule out that this party had a vested interest and was involved in the return of the archive, just as it was involved earlier in its concealment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Asked and answered, and it's your statement. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked, but Mr. Blaszczyk answered a question I didn't put. I asked if he ruled out the possibility by usual means, usual methods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the Defence team of any of the accused involved or present in this hand-over of documentation? Just answer with a yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the question, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was a representative of Republika Srpska present in Zagreb when this hand-over to you was done, or repackaging maybe?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The archive was transported by UN car with UN escort to -- directly to our office in Zagreb. Nobody was present from RS side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This documentation was repacked at least twice, perhaps three times; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you sure that you have received all the documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that we haven't received all documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. And are you sure that no documents were subsequently added? In other words, did you receive a protocol and were you able to compare to make sure that the documents you were receiving were recorded contemporaneously either as incoming or outgoing?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We never received such documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you cannot rule out the possibility that some of the documents that could affect one or more accused have been concealed before the hand-over to you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, we cannot rule out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also cannot rule out the possibility that some exculpatory documents, exculpatory to other accused, were also removed before the hand-over to you?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot exclude possibility that some documents were removed from the archive. What kind of documents they will be, we don't know. We know for sure that we are still lacking of documents from security department or security branch of VRS. We are quite lacking the documents of -- logistic documents relating to July period, let's say, 1995. Some operational documents are missing. What else, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Blaszczyk. I'm finished, Your Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just one topic, Mr. Blaszczyk. There were some questions about -- quite a few questions about where the U-turn was made, how you know where the U-turn was made when Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Petrovic were travelling on the 13th of July in the vicinity of Sandici/Konjevic Polje. I want to just try to keep this clear, play some of the video again. It won't take long.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go to 14:30, please, and this will be relevant to map book page 36. You can play from 14:30.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get a time reference, the time of day when this was filmed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have time reference at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There's no -- he can see as well as we can when the counter appears and when it doesn't, so I'd rather just keep playing it at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've stopped at 15:01.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, this photo corresponds -- this still corresponds just about perfectly with picture D on page 36 of the road book which you've marked as position on map 10. Now, which direction is Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Pirocanac travelling at this time and where are they?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Pirocanac, they are following with their car these two APCs we see on this footage. They are driving towards the direction of Konjevic Polje. They're slowly moving towards the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, we won't repeat your testimony but you established that by the houses and the topography and the sequence of the video; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Keep playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry. We stopped at 16:27.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The previous footage we saw was from outside the car. We're now in the car moving; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Keep playing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We're now at 16:28.12 -- sorry, 16:32.3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a counter on my screen. I can't understand why I don't see the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm speaking, Mr. Karadzic, of the red counter in the bottom right on the Sanction presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, this still corresponds to photos -- to photo A on page 38 of the map book which you've marked as map -- as position on map 11, 2.000 metres from Sandici meadow on the road leading from Konjevic Polje towards Sandici and Bratunac. Can you tell us -- look at this. Where are we now in this video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said, we are about 2.000 metres from Sandici meadow, and the car is approaching Sandici meadow. In a few minutes they will be in Sandici meadow, near Sandici meadow. This is area called Pervani, Lolici nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So what we're seeing now, is this before or after the U-turn that was made?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after U-turn they made, and this is first footage recorded by Mr. Pirocanac when they made U-turn. Where exactly they made U-turn we don't know because as we saw the footage previously, the Pervani, these two APCs, the footage was recorded about 100 metres -- 1.000 metres from this place towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And this is the location where we see the reference of Mr. Borovcanin and Oficir, if we keep playing another minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Stopped at 16:48.0.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So map position 11, which is shown -- described on page 38 of the map book. Is this where the discussion is taking place with Borovcanin and Oficir?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question. Was this the first contact between Borovcanin and his unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean between Borovcanin and his unit? Borovcanin was the commanding officer of the police forces in this area. I don't believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we can read the transcript if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I was just going to say that doesn't arise from my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. But this is not the part that you referred to as his -- as his receiving reports as to the wound -- the wounding of Oficir, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is Oficir. His name -- his real name is Cuturic. I think Rade Cuturic. He was the man who was wounded in Kravica warehouse, in this incident in Kravica warehouse, but later on as we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. No. He was wounded later on during -- when the Kravica started from the shooting of and killing of one of the Serb policemen over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: According to your evidence, Mr. Borovcanin made a stop at Sandici still after having heard his -- Oficir was wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think they're talking about totally different events now. There is not conversation about his wounds here. I believe that Oficir, Cuturic, is still in good shape here, when they have conversation on the radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember the second portion of Sandici Mr. Pirocanac took before they arrived in the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When they were at Sandici for the second time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- had Mr. Borovcanin have heard about Oficir's injury?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could hear. Could hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that was my --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened near this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- question. I'm sorry, I overlapped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my fault. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, could hear. Thank you. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Blaszczyk. Thank you for your testimony again. Now you are free to go, but could you bear with me. There's a very brief short ruling the Chamber wishes to issue now. Immediately after the recent filing of the "Sixth Order on Chart of Protective Measures for Witnesses," it was brought to the Chamber's attention that the protective measures in place for two of the witnesses referred to in the chart, KDZ494 and KDZ515, have been augmented in other proceedings, and that the protective measures for KDZ555 have been varied, also in other proceedings. The Chamber recalls the Prosecution's obligation to "immediately inform the Chamber and the accused when there is a variation of the protective measures in place for any of the witnesses in the chart." The Chamber therefore orders that Prosecution provide accurate information as to the protective measures currently in place for witnesses KDZ494, KDZ515, and KDZ555, no later than Monday, 30 January 2012. The Chamber takes this opportunity to reiterate that it is absolutely crucial for the Prosecution to keep an accurate record to all variations to protective measures of witnesses in this case and to inform the Chamber accordingly. We'll take a break now for half an hour and resume at 1 -- 10 to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ruez. Could you make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Could you please state and spell your full name.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My name is Jean-Rene Ruez, R-u-e-z.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Before we start, can you just describe what that material is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a book that was handed to me by the Prosecution and that has all the photographs related to events I'm supposed to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the other sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's the list of the main witnesses with their code-name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, we've provided Mr. Ruez with the pseudonyms of the witnesses who he will be referring to in the course of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, what is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I am -- I am chief superintendent in the French national police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And going back about 15 years, you worked for the Office of the Prosecutor from the 7th of April, 1995, to the 7th of April 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And for part of that time you were the team leader for the Srebrenica investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come to that in a minute, but if you can just briefly outline for us your educational background and then your career in the French police force.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I joined the police as a superintendent in 1986. I worked for the judicial police until I joined the Tribunal in April 1995, so until 2001, and after that I took a leave of absence for two years and then worked for the directorate of an international corporation first in Paris. And since 2008, I am working for -- as a police attache in a French embassy abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is it correct that you also did a year of military service at some stage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I was a reserve officer. I did my military service as an officer in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And you've also completed a law degree; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. That was in 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, coming to when you joined the Office of the Prosecutor in April 1995, how did that come about? How was it that you came to join the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There was an appeal for volunteers, and I applied in 1994 and was recruited in 1995. I was initially in a team investigating the siege of Sarajevo, and in July 1995, as soon as the enclave fell, I was tasked to go in the area and start investigation that was connected with the press rumours about the disappearance of thousands of men. And I never stopped working on this investigation until my -- my departure in April 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: When did you first go to the area of Srebrenica after you heard those press rumours?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I was sent there -- I think I arrived in Tuzla area in -- on or about 20 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The first step was to find out what had happened, so by interviewing witnesses who came from that area, from the Srebrenica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you briefly outline for us the phases that the investigation went through in the following years up to your departure in April 2001?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I often compare this investigation to the construction of a house, where you need first to have foundations, then build the walls and at the end build the roof. So the first phase was to reconstruct the events in their chronology, so by interviewing witnesses who escaped from the area, including the top witnesses who claimed having survived mass executions, but also the UN personnel who were in the enclave as well as collecting all open sources on the topic including videos. The second phase, the construction of the walls, is to corroborate or infirm [sic] the declarations of these witnesses, so by finding the locations we're talking about, so mainly detention sites. Also then the execution sites, the initial burial spots of the ones that we call the primary mass graves, and since these graves had been disturbed, also find and identify them as such the secondary mass graves. Once this could be achieved then came the final phase, the roof, meaning the identification of the perpetrators by a process of conducting searches in military facilities in order to collect documentation, but also recover all the available intercepts, communication intercepts that were done during the time of the events, and also getting into an interview process of the military personnel suspected to be involved as well as police personnel. So at the end, once these phases are completed, the heating system can be activated, which is indictments and bringing to justice these indictees and the trial phase.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You mentioned searches in military facilities. I want to ask you briefly about two of them. First the Bratunac Brigade. Can you describe to us how the Office of the Prosecutor first came across that site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We came across the Bratunac Brigade in the early stages, in 1996, but the situation was at that time absolutely not ripe enough to be able to conduct any search in this location. So, alike the Zvornik Brigade, who were the two -- the two brigades most likely to be suspect, this search could only be done in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you seize anything when you went to the Bratunac Brigade in 1996?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We took most of the records from the headquarters, but we quickly found out through the military analysis of all what was captured there that the -- the main archives connected with July 1995 were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what about the initial search in 1996? Did you seize anything at all when you went there then?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, we -- we searched a container that was outside of the HQ and seized a bunch of blue helmets which were located there and that had been taken from the UN soldiers when the enclave was taken over by the Bosnian Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And final question on this area. What was the security situation like in those early years, 1995, 1996, 1997?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The security situation was - how could I say? - volatile. For sure I mean the peace was officially implemented, but nevertheless, all the military structures of those involved in the summer 1995 events were still around, as well as the local political personnel and also the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I turn your attention now to the book of photos that's in front of you. What is this book, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's the book with all the photographs we are going to go through together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Who took these photos, and who selected them for this book?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I took most of them, as well as did the maps which are in them. This is a selection that was made for previous trials and then has been expurged of some which are less relevant for this case, but I didn't do the selection for this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn to photo 1 in the book. That's page 11 in e-court. Or map number 1. Sorry, it's 65 ter 3199. Mr. Ruez, we're looking at a map that's covering the area from Zeleni Jadar in the south up to Kula in the north. Is this map to scale?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is to scale. The scale is bottom right. This map shows, in fact, the entire -- entire area where the events took place from north to south. It's more or less the size of the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And just around where that blue box is in the bottom right-hand corner, you see a faint grey line in the same area. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This is the area where the UN safe area of Srebrenica was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page, photo 2, page 12, in e-court. Mr. Ruez, if you can explain what's in this photograph and which direction we're looking at it from?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So this photograph shows the -- part of the Srebrenica town seen from the south, coming from Zeleni Jadar towards Srebrenica town. So how to see, but it is a stretched town in between two -- two hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: How far is it from Potocari to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Approximately 5K.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And do you recall when this photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The one at the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's photo number 2?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, photo number 2 and maybe also number 3, they were not taken on the same mission, but the one on the right, the number 3, is 1998. It's a photograph that I took from a helicopter that shows the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If I can stop you there. Why don't we go to the next page, photo number 3, page 13 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's another view of the town to -- to show the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So as we can see in the top, heading towards the top right-hand corner of the picture, the town is disappearing into the distance. What direction that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the direction of Potocari and then Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn to the next page, photo number 4. Actually, the next two pages in your book are maps. If you can explain what we're looking at in this map and what the significance of the green arrow is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this map shows the situation that happened at moment of the fall of the enclave, 11 July 1995. A large group of people decided to leave the -- the enclave, and they took the direction of the north of the safe area, an area named Susnjari, where they gathered waiting for the night and with the intent then to -- to cross the line and flee the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what's the basis of your knowledge that people went to that area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is based on the interviews of those who took the -- who were among those who took the decision to -- not to stay but attempted to leave the area. This group is assessed to be approximately made of 15.000 people, at least a third of them being the members of the 28th Division, which was the military unit inside the enclave and still military equipped despite of official demilitarisation of the place. The rest being unarmed [Realtime transcript read in error "armed"] civilians for most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. And if you can explain to us briefly what that grey shaded line is and the yellow lettered dots that we can see.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The -- the grey line is the, in brackets, boundary of this safe area, which had no official boundary but it was a de facto boundary. And the yellow dots spot the observation points of the UN force inside the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next map, page 5 in the book and page 15 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this -- this situation -- this map shows the other course of action that was taken by those who stayed inside the enclave when it fell. And this mass of people decided to find some security by getting close to the UN base that was located in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. We're going to look at a short video now. It's 65 ter 40063, and we just have a short excerpt of that. Mr. Ruez, we're going to play this without sound, and if you can just describe to us what we're seeing as we watch this video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is a helicopter film showing how the area looks like. This is filmed coming from south to north, so from Zeleni Jadar towards Srebrenica town. The -- the road that one can see is the -- the road that the Bosnian Serb Army took to enter the area. So this is the overflying of the Srebrenica town, embedded between these hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And which direction are we looking in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: From south to north. So at this moment flying above centre town in the direction of Potocari, and then it continues on a straight line nearly towards Bratunac. This is the centre town. And now flying towards Potocari. This is the building of the UN base, the Bravo Company. And this is the direction of Potocari and totally at the distance would be Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I tender at that clip, please, Mr. President. It's 65 ter 40063A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P4279, Your Honours. THE PROSECUTOR:

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, just one transcript clarification. At page 68, line 4, you were talking about the column of 15.000 people in Susnjari and you said that at least a third of them being the members of the 28th Division. "The rest being armed civilians for the most of them." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, it is not. What I said is that the rest of them were for most of them unarmed civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go back to 65 ter 3199 and go to page 14 in e-court. That's photo number 4. My apologies. Page 16 in e-court and photo 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we switch to e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you tell us what this black and white image is and where the investigation got it from.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is an aerial photograph provided by the US showing the location of Potocari on which I did put the yellow markings in order to identify the -- mainly -- the mostly locations witnesses refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Who put the date on that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The date was on the initial photograph we received through the US State Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And does this apply to the other aerial images we're going to look at, that the header and the date come from the provider?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. All -- all what will be on inside white frames will be on the -- is on the initial photograph provided by the US.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page, photo 7, page 17 in e-court. Now, starting with the object circled in white in the middle of the photo, can you describe what that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This is the -- the place that we always refer to as the white house. This is a detention site, I think the detention site in Potocari. During the deportation of the population, there was a line of soldiers who were separating the men from their families, and these men were taken to this location, and from there, group after groups put on board of buses to be taken in detention at Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what's the basis of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Several persons who ended up surviving went through this place. The selection process was done under the eyes -- the separation process, sorry, under the eyes of the UN soldiers. We also have video footage of the men who were identified by name later on and who were marched towards -- towards this location. This location was also visited by UN military observer, Major Kingori from Kenya, who entered this location together with General Mladic who was on the spot that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just orient us on this picture. The -- starting with the road down the very bottom in the left-hand corner. Where is this road coming from?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the bottom of the picture, the road is coming from Srebrenica towards Potocari, leading to this big building which was a battery factory before the war, and then the road continues towards Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And that's up in the top right-hand corner of the photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. It's the blue box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 18 in e-court. It's photo number 8. And, Mr. Ruez, if you can firstly tell us what this is and then what time of year this photo was taken.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This photo shows the -- it's another view of the so-called white house. It is the first picture of it that I could take from the ground. It was a mission done in wintertime, as you can see, in January 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, photo 9, and page 19, in e-court. We're going to see a split image. Mr. Ruez, if you can explain the significance of this split image.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Before we could access the photograph on the top, we had no material evidence that could confirm the testimonies saying that there were prisoners in this house that was so full that, as Major Kingori said, the people are sitting on top each of another, and also the balcony was used to store these men. The photo at the bottom shows the location where the men are filmed at the top, and the picture at the top is one of the ones we named "the lost pictures." There was a Serb journalist from Studio B on the -- in the area when the enclave fell. We could access his footage, that is labelled V550 by the Prosecution, but in which Zoran Petkovic, the journalist, did initially cut off all the bits that could assist the Tribunal to better understand the situation and all those that were connected with ongoing crimes or future crimes were erased by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, that reference to V550, that's an ERN number; is that correct? That's the Prosecution's ERN number?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The V550?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it's the Prosecution number of the entire footage of Zoran Petrovic without -- I mean, with the cuts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go to page 10. That's page 20 in e-court. And this is another map. And now we can see a black arrow pointing from Potocari towards Bratunac. What does this arrow show?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This arrow shows the direction taken by the men who were separated and taken to the white house during 12 and 13 July, who were taken to Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please go to the next page, photo 11, and page 21 in e-court. If you can describe what this aerial image shows.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This one shows the first detention spot where the prisoners were taken to, which is, in fact, the Vuk Karadzic school complex in Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What's the specific name of that building that's circled in blue?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a hangar that is just behind the school. This is the location where one of the survivors was taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And how did you first come to learn about this hangar?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Several witnesses talked about the school area, and when we went there, we also found this hangar that seemed to match with the description made by one survivor and who confirmed the fact that this was indeed the place he had been kept inside when we showed him the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page. I think it's photo 12. The next one, sorry. Number 13, page 23 in e-court. If you can describe what this structure is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a ground view of the hangar we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Are there other buildings of significance to the investigation that are located nearby to this hangar?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. I think we'll go through them at a later stage, but there are three buildings of relevance just in this place; the first one being the Vuk Karadzic school, next to it a gym, and at the right of this photograph is another building that is named the older school, which is a technical school. All these places having been used for detaining prisoners. Since these places were full, many of them stayed during the night on board of buses and trucks that were lined in several locations in Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. Do you recall when this photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. It's visible at the bottom right of the picture I have. I don't know if it is visible on the screen, but it is in June 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we move to the map on page 14, page 24 in e-court. Mr. Ruez, what we see now is a map with a black arrow pointing from the Susnjari area towards Konjevic Polje. What does this indicate?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the direction of flight of those who fled the area. They started the journey during the night between the 11 and the 12. Most of the 28th Division left first, the civilians following behind. It was a long column since they first went through an opening made in a minefield, and this column stretched along this area of hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If I can just stop you there. What is this terrain like? Can you describe that to us? Between Susnjari and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We could have a feeling of how it looks like when we saw the video from helicopter. It's -- it's a hilly area in this location, and this column in fact walked behind a hill line all along the road that goes from Bratunac towards the -- the west direction, Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to the next page, page 15, page 25 in e-court. If you can describe the significance of the yellow arrow that we see towards the top of the picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: As I just said, in fact, you can see at the bottom first the road, the asphalt road that goes from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, and the column of those who were fleeing went behind this -- this hill so to be out of sight of the military forces that were along this road. So behind the hills towards the direction of Konjevic Polje. That was during the 12th July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page. Photo 16, page 26 in e-court. If you can explain first the arrow pointing towards Nova Kasaba, what that means.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So this is the last hill before arriving at the intersection of Konjevic Polje where the asphalt road turns to the south in direction of Nova Kasaba and to the north direction Zvornik. So this is the place where this column intended to cross the asphalt road. The -- the big army group at the front was successful doing that on the evening of the 12th July, but those who were behind did not make this crossing because of military reinforcements, and so all this large group was trapped behind and for many of them were blocked on top of this big hill on the -- on the photograph, those others being far behind, not having even reached this spot by the end of the 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What's the name of the area where this hill is that we can see on the left? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's -- I don't know if it has a specific name. We call it the hill overlooking Konjevici, Konjevici being the area where the village Konjevic Polje is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And where exactly -- which direction would the Konjevic Polje intersection be in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's at the west of Bratunac at approximately 15 kilometres from -- from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And on this photo can you see the actual intersection?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On this one that is on the screen, no, because it is -- it would be just at the -- at the right of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So is the black arrow that is pointing towards the Konjevic Polje intersection, is that pointing in the right direction or is the intersection actually the other way?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No. In fact, the -- it points towards the intersection, but by continuing to the left where it is written "Konjevic Polje intersection," this goes to Bratunac, and at Konjevic Polje you have another direction that goes towards Zvornik. We will see that more clearly on the following photograph, 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next photograph. It's page 27 in e-court. And if you can explain to us firstly what this group of houses is that we see on the right. What's that called?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this view is the one one has when being on the hill, not on the top but at the bottom of the hill, where you can see on the right the asphalt road going towards the north, the top of the picture, would lead to go towards Zvornik --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sorry, if I can stop you there. What about the road going to the right of the picture? Where does that take you to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The bottom right is the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And to the left?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: And the bottom left is the direction of Nova Kasaba. The arrow, the yellow arrow points the direction that was one of the spearhead of the column. It is crossing this asphalt road and going then to -- continuing to the east towards the valley of Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to the Cerska Valley shortly. If we can go to the next page, page 18, page 28 in e-court. This is a map called "Prisoners of war, regroupment sites, 13 July 1995." Can you explain what aspect of the investigation this map relates to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So on 13 July the two processes are finalised, one being the capture of the prisoners, the situation I described, for example, in Potocari. Then you also have the end of the deportation process that was during the 12 and the 13, where the people were shipped towards Muslim-held territory at Kladanj. That is completely at the left of the photograph -- of the map. So in the west direction. Where another process of separation of men who had managed to get on board of buses took place. And you mainly have that day a massive surrender process of all those who were among this -- this column of men fleeing towards Konjevic Polje and who in the morning of the following days, or the 13, surrendered massively to the Serb forces who were all along this asphalt road going along from Bratunac to Nova Kasaba. So this map shows the main spots where these prisoners were initially kept that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what's the first of those sites that we're going to look at in the following pages?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the first one is on page 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go over one more page. That's page 29 in e-court. I think we can see the blue dot on the very far left of the picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is that the first site that we're going to look at?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This spot is just at the -- at the east of the line of Kladanj, which is the separation line between RS and BiH, and the men who were separated at this final spot before reaching the Muslim-held territory were taken to an elementary school which is named the Luke school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, how did you first become aware that men had been held at the Luke school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This information came from one man who had been taken to this location and who further survived the events and could testify about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is his name on that list in front of you, and if so, would you able to read out his pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. He is the witness KDZ070.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go to page 20 in the book, page 30 in e-court. Mr. Ruez, if you can explain to us what this building is that we see here.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So this building along the road that leads, if we would continue this road, leads to the direction of Kladanj. So the men came from this road and were taken to this small building which is the elementary school of Luke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: How did you find the school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We drove to this area together with the witness I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what year was that, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I'm not sure but it was quite late. It was -- it might be in 1998, I'm not hundred per cent sure. It could be 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, in the Srebrenica trial video which the Trial Chamber has seen, there's footage of a drop-off point in Luke where the people were dropped off the buses and walked to Kladanj. How far is this school from that drop-off point?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Maybe 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, page 21 in the hard copy, 31 in e-court. What are we looking at in this photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a rear view of this little building that shows the position that the witness designated to me when he explained that initially the group in which he was was sitting in between the two trees at the left of the photograph before being taken inside the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So just to be clear, this is a photo of the school. That's the school building on the left of the photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to the next page, page 22, page 32 in e-court. And what does this photo show?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This photograph shows the classroom that he describes where he was held together with others and where he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that might be a good place to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mitchell, given that we should adjourn tomorrow at 1.15, so with the indulgence of the staff, we may go today until quarter past 2.00 if parties do not object. Half an hour more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's fine from our end, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, would it be okay with you as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perfectly okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go it page 23 in the book, page 33 in e-court. If you can tell us what next site is that we're going look at.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is another area where prisoners were initially regrouped in the area of Nova Kasaba where there are two main spots of initial detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page, 24 in the book, 34 in e-court. Now, this is another aerial image. It says "Buses at facility, Nova Kasaba, 13 July 1995." Now, this image also has a time on it. Can you explain what that wavy line in front of the time means.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The wavy line indicates that it's an approximate time, approximately 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what's the significance of this site in the photo? What's its significance to the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So it is a location that was the base of the 65th Protection Regiment of the Bosnian Serb Army. Dutch soldiers were kept inside, and this is how we know that it was also used as a detention site, and in front of them one can also see the presence of three buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And just to clarify, did you put those yellow markings on this image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page, page 25, page 35 in e-court. And if you can describe what we can see in this photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken from the road at that goes from Nova Kasaba, in fact, to -- more to the south, to a little town named Milici, and this is a ground view of the building we could see on the aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Page 28 and page 38 in e-court, please. We're looking at another aerial image here. Mr. Ruez, can you explain what, if anything, is significant about this particular image.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's at page 28. Okay. It is a close shot of what is in fact, but we will see it better on other pictures, a football pitch. It's a football pitch squared by a tree line all around. And the grey areas, one rectangle and one thin rectangle at the left of this football pitch are groups of people which, in fact, are the prisoners who have surrendered in this area and have been brought to this soccer field of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Whose conclusion is that at the top of the image where it says "People at football field"? Was that your conclusion or was that put on there by the provider?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It was put on the picture by the provider, and it matches testimonies that we have on the spot, and it also matches the observations that we could have on the spot when figuring out the size of these dots compared with the size a man would have on this aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So is the right direction to the -- to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And left being to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The left towards Nova Kasaba. The intersection being at the right towards Konjevic Polje and then it's in Konjevic Polje that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you see page 27, e-court 37?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, it's correct that the football field we see here is located on the Konjevic Polje-Milici road?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Before Milici and before Nova Kasaba. Nova Kasaba is at the left of the road maybe 1 -- 1 kilometre left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And if you kept following the photo we're looking at now, photo 27, if you followed that road down where it exits out the bottom right, where would that lead you to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That would lead to the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: And then turning right towards Bratunac and going straight would go towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to page 29, 39 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What bus convoy does this refer to then? Can you go back to page 27.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the buses that can be seen on the road are buses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's moving from -- they are moving from where to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two options. Either are they moving at this moment, because it's the 13th, still evacuating people from the enclave towards Kladanj. In that case they would be full of people, but we cannot see. And the other option, they return empty from Kladanj towards Srebrenica to continue -- to continue the deportation process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you go back to page 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's page 33 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please. So the football pitch is the bigger circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The small circle is the 26 -- 56th Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 65th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 65th, and the big circle is the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go back to page 29, page 39 in e-court. If you can briefly describe this photo to us, or first can you orient us on this road that we can see running up the middle.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: As the road heads out the top of the picture, where does that go to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At the top it goes to Nova Kasaba, and at the bottom towards the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what's the -- the area we see on the right-hand side of the picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is a helicopter photograph -- photograph taken from a helicopter of the same football pitch we could see on the aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go to the next photo now, 30, and page 40 in e-court. What does this photo show, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On -- this photo it was taken in April 1996. The man on the photo is, in fact, dog handlers of the Bosnian Serb Army. It shows how it was at the early stages. The interest of them is to make sure that the grey zones marked as people are indeed not vegetation as one defendant previously implied this would be. There are no trees or whatsoever on this football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go to page 31 now, page 41 in e-court. And this is another map we're about to see, and we can see a blue dot near Konjevic Polje. Can you describe what the next site we're going to look at is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is an additional regroupment site in this area which is precisely located at the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And how did you learn of this particular site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mainly through one witness who was taken to that spot and later survived to report about what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you see his witness code on that list in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. He is KDZ065. 065.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to the next page. It's page 32, number 42 in e-court. Mr. Ruez, this is another aerial image dated 27 July 1995. Can you explain the significance of the blue circle in the very centre of the photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is an aerial photograph of a military facility just -- just at the very short distance, I mean, let's say, 400 or 500 metres away from the intersection. It is the first spot where the witness I just referred to was taken. He was taken initially to the guardhouse of this unit, which is the 5th Engineer Battalion of the Bosnian Serb Army, and from there he was taken to a few other spots of this -- in this facility but which are not relevant to enter into detail on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you go to the site with this witness?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We redo -- we redid the circuit that he was made to do that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, photo 33, page 43 in e-court. If you can explain what this building is that we can see in the photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. This is the ground view of the entrance of the 5th Engineer Battalion with the little guardhouse at the left of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, please, page 34, page 44 in e-court. If you can describe this photo to us, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So from the 5th Engineer Battalion, the witness and a group of people with who he was surrendering were taken to what he names a warehouse at the intersection. When we came with him, there was no more -- no longer any warehouse but it's replaced by a gas station. But from a photograph I took in April 1996, we will see it on another picture, this one is from April 1997, but at that time the hangar was still there and it is indeed the one where he was taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And you said this is at the intersection. Which intersection is this, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So the road leading to the right of the picture goes in which direction?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The road to the right where the blue line is goes to the right to Bratunac. Once at the intersection to the left to Nova Kasaba and to the top towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, page 35, 45 in e-court. And if you can briefly describe to us what this building on the left of the photo is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the so-called hangar in -- at the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And just to be clear, this initial visit, the witness wasn't with you at this time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, correct. He was not with us. It was the -- I mean, whether -- I didn't take this picture for the sake of this demonstration. It was someone -- a picture that I found later on but where the hangar is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to another site, page 36 in your book, page 46 in e-court. Now, which site are the next series of photos related to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the main site of gathering of prisoners during the day of 13 July. It's the so-called Sandici area. There were a few spots of surrendering in this place, but all these prisoners were taken initially to Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Well, let's move to the next page, page 37, 47 in e-court. And if you can explain just briefly what significance of these two yellow markings are.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. This is -- this photograph is to show precisely where a scene of the video V550 was shot and on which one can see people in the surrender process coming from the top of this hill. On the V550 you can see them coming at the top of the hill in the yellow rectangle at the right and also visible on the video the electric pylon which is circled in yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And that V550 is the Zoran Petrovic footage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Could we please go to next page, page 38, 48 in e-court. Now there's two photos on this page. Could you explain to us what we're looking at in these two images.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this is the view from close to the asphalt road where the Bosnian Serb was present, and the men were on the top of the hills, and they took the path that can be seen on the photograph at the right, the path down in order to surrender at this -- at this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: When were these photos taken, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
